subject: Creating interaction terms with NA using IndProd

messages.author: 4f373f746900e389
messages.subject: Creating interaction terms with NA using IndProd
parts:
Hi all,

I know this is a very basic question but I am a bit stuck at the moment, which is why I thought it is wise to consult this group. I have not found anything on how to deal with missing values when using the IndProd function.

I have missing values in my variables and if I compute the interaction term using this variable, it is logical that NAs in my interaction terms are returned. I have to tell R that it should ignore missing values. How can I do that in my code?

This is my code:

Dataset <- indProd(Dataset , var1 = c("x1", x2", "x3", "x4" ), var2 = c("y1"))

Thanks a lot for your help!!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Creating interaction terms with NA using IndProd
parts: I have missing values in my variables and if I compute the interaction term using this variable, it is logical that NAs in my interaction terms are returned.
I have to tell R that it should ignore missing values.

What do you mean?  That contradicts your previous sentence.  Anything times NA is NA.  The product indicators should be missing whenever either variable is missing, which is what indProd() will give you.
